content.text: The spec has no data model, screen, stored data or artifacts, so there are no entities, fields, views or persistence to design. Reuse gate: nothing to look up, because the spec names no noun that could be an entity. The feature is one stateless Java class,
, plus its input and result types.
: attendees as a list of busy-time lists, and busy times as start–end pairs. Working hours are one start–end pair. The meeting length is in minutes. Times are
, which fits the one-day, no-time-zone scope. Busy time and working hours can share one small immutable
value type (start, end, end after start).
: "no slot" is a value, not an exception and not a bare null, so callers cannot confuse it with the rejected-input error (R5, R7). The result is
, and an empty optional means no slot.
: a null input, an empty attendee list, a length of zero or less, a busy time or working hours whose end is not after its start. All of these throw
for null, and return no result. Validation runs before any computation.
rejects end ≤ start at construction. The finder checks the null, empty-list and length cases itself.
Clip every busy time to the working hours. Busy time wholly outside has no effect (R3).

Merge all attendees' clipped busy times into one list. An attendee with no busy times adds nothing (R6). Sort by start and merge ranges that overlap or touch (end ≥ next start) into blocks (R2). Sorting and merging make the result independent of input order (P1).
Walk the free gaps in order, starting with the gap from the working-hours start to the first block, and ending with the gap after the last block.
In each gap, the candidate start is the gap start rounded UP to the next 15-minute step (R4, R8).
The first candidate with candidate + length ≤ gap end, and so within the working hours, is the answer (R1, R3). Slot length is exactly the given minutes (R8).
If no gap fits, return empty (R5).
: steps are measured from midnight (:00, :15, :30, :45). The working-hours start itself may be off-step. In that case the first slot starts at the next step.
: the class has no fields and no side effects, so it is safe to share. The same input always gives the same answer (P1).
Acceptance examples A1–A15 map one-to-one to unit tests. Each test name carries its A-number, and the A13 cases are parameterised.
